currentContext.business: Indegene helps biopharma, emerging biotech and medical technology companies modernize and scale commercialization operations across five core pillars - Discovery & Evidence, Regulatory & Compliance, Commercial Launch, Content & Engagement, and Patient & Outcomes - combining deep life sciences domain expertise with AI-embedded platforms and governed operating models. The Company positions itself as neither a life sciences IT company, a horizontal outsourcer, a specialty agency nor a CRO, but as a domain-deep platform that takes accountability for regulated workflows and the business outcomes they deliver. As of March 31, 2026 it served all of the world's top 20 biopharma companies and 91 active clients, operating in more than 80 markets through 17+ delivery and operational centers across 11 countries with over 5,500 professionals.

AI platforms and data layer: Cortex (life sciences-native, LLM-agnostic reasoning engine encoding domain expertise in semantic knowledge graphs)
Mesh of expert AI agents (creative content, medical writing, medico-legal review, safety monitoring, HCP journey optimization, submissions planning)
Cockpit of domain experts orchestrating regulated workflows
Tandem data platform (added through the BioPharm acquisition)
Next-generation AI-embedded operating mo: Agentic AOR (Agency of Record) of the Future
Tectonic (GenAI-embedded 'agency-of-scale' model for creative development, adaptation and execution)

currentContext.expansion: Indegene's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than plant-and-machinery led. During FY 2025-26 the Company completed three strategic acquisitions to strengthen capabilities and expand presence in key geographies. BioPharm, acquired in October 2025, strengthened omnichannel data and targeting capabilities within the enterprise commercial segment through the addition of the Tandem data platform; its integration was completed ahead of schedule by the end of February 2026, with synergies on general and administrative expense, data subscriptions, business operations and go-to-market progressively unlocking through FY 2026-27. Alongside BioPharm, the Company acquired Warn & Co and Cake Kommunikations - additions of people with deep expertise and local market knowledge in key European geographies that complement the global delivery model in Europe with on-the-ground credibility and relationships. Physical footprint expansion has been through global delivery centers: new centers opened in London, Pune and Mumbai, a new global delivery center in Noida, an earlier delivery center in Hyderabad, a strategic center in Germany, a new entity launched in Spain and a China operation center at Shanghai and Dalian - taking the network to 17+ delivery and operational centers across 11 countries serving more than 80 markets, supported by hubs and offices across North America, Europe and Asia. The Company also continued to invest in senior leadership and thought-leadership talent across commercial and medical leadership to engage at C-suite level for larger transformation mandates, and in building and scaling category-defining technology platforms and GenAI-embedded solutions (Cortex and the solutions built on it). Forward capex/expansion intent stated in the Business Outlook is to keep investing in AI, proprietary platforms, domain expertise and consulting capabilities, and to expand across therapeutic areas and geographies while selectively pursuing capability-led acquisitions. No rupee capex budget, plant capacity or commissioning schedule is disclosed.

risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of global biopharma buyers
risks.note: 58.5% of revenues are derived from the top 20 global biopharma companies, and the client base is only 91 active clients; a budget cut, vendor consolidation or loss at one or two large accounts would be disproportionately felt.

risks.risk: Dependence on global life sciences industry operating spend
risks.note: The Company states its revenue performance is closely aligned with global life sciences industry spending on operations, so the top line moves with client commercialization budgets rather than with an independent demand cycle.

risks.risk: Pharma patent cliff and loss of exclusivity by 2030
risks.note: A wave of blockbuster patent expiries exposes clients to generic and biosimilar competition on a scale rarely seen, pressuring the commercial budgets that Indegene's work is embedded in - even as it also creates the modernization demand the Company sells into.

risks.risk: Technology / AI disruption of the work Indegene itself performs
risks.note: The Company's thesis is that generic foundation models cannot reason about regulated life sciences workflows; if that domain moat narrows, or if clients build in-house, the pricing power of an outcome-based model built on AI-driven efficiency erodes. Management explicitly ties competitiveness to embedding AI faster than the industry.

risks.risk: Data privacy, PII handling and information security across regulated client workflows
risks.note: The business processes HCP and patient-linked data in regulated environments; risk management is built around privacy impact assessments (PIA/DPIA), PII asset and data-flow registers, Records of Processing Activities, an enterprise-wide network of Privacy Champions and continuous security-awareness and phishing-resilience programs, indicating the exposure is treated as material.

A structured Third-Party Risk Management programme aligned to ISO/IEC 27036, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 31000 governs the vendor lifecycle - reflecting reliance on external technology, data-subscription and delivery partners in an accountable, regulated delivery chain.

risks.risk: Talent attrition and dependence on scarce domain-plus-AI specialists
risks.note: Delivery rests on over 5,500 professionals including more than 1,500 life sciences specialists; voluntary turnover for permanent employees was 16.35% in FY 2025-26 (17.13% in FY 2024-25), and the judgement-intensive work cannot be staffed generically.

risks.risk: Near-total export revenue concentration and cross-border regulatory exposure
risks.note: Exports contributed 98.47% of turnover in FY 2025-26 (98.27% in FY 2024-25, including inter-company revenue), leaving earnings exposed to currency movements, cross-border tax/regulatory change and client-country policy shifts.

risks.risk: Climate change and GHG emissions as an ESG-linked commercial risk
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material issue: although a digital-first services company has a lower direct footprint, office operations, purchased electricity, business travel and cloud/data-centre usage plus rising climate expectations from global life sciences clients mean failure to monitor and reduce emissions could affect client expectations, ESG ratings, competitiveness in ESG-sensitive client bids and regulatory preparedness.

one-line thesis: Indegene crossed ₹1,000cr quarterly revenue for the first time, driven by GenAI-enabled outcome contracts and deepening top-20 pharma relationships, while reported PAT dipped due to a one-time legal provision and forex hedge accounting changes. The strategic pivot from 'IT services' to 'strategic operating partner' is validating via multi-year deals (Tectonic, Omnichannel) that shift spend from agencies/CROs to Indegene, setting up margin recovery and accelerated growth in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹10,000mn (Q4, +32.8% YoY), ₹35,105mn (FY26, +23.6% YoY); EBITDA: ₹1,889mn adjusted Q4 (+23.2% YoY), ₹6,793mn FY26 (+20.8% YoY) vs ₹1,648mn reported Q4 due to ₹241mn forex hedge charge; PAT: ₹797mn Q4, ₹4,011mn FY26 (-1.4% YoY) vs ₹4,583mn normalized (+12.7% YoY) after excluding ₹203mn TCPA lawsuit provision and forex adjustments; Order Book: Strong momentum with 7 deals >$1mn ACV in Q4, including $10mn+ omnichannel deal (revenue deferred to FY27) and Tectonic Germany win; Net Debt: Net Cash position ~₹15,385mn (Cash & Investments), Free Cash Flow ₹6,065mn FY26.
guidance: No formal revenue guidance; management expresses 'excited and confident' tone for FY27 citing larger/balanced pipeline, Tectonic scaling, and conversion of pilots to platforms; expects EBITDA margins to revert to pre-investment levels in H2FY27 as 150bps investment impact absorbs; PAT expected to see significant upward movement in FY27 as one-offs fade and amortization stabilizes.
order book & pipeline: Q4 bookings include 1 deal >$3mn ACV (clinical, new customer), 7 deals >$1mn ACV (4 from top-20); Key wins: Tectonic engagement (Germany, largest customer), $10mn+ multiyear omnichannel deal (revenue recognition in FY27), end-to-end commercialization for mid-sized biotech, global pharmacovigilance for medical devices client, global innovation center pilot for $100bn+ cap company.
segment / subsidiary detail: Enterprise Commercial (ex-BioPharm): +17% YoY; Enterprise Medical Services (EMS): +16% YoY; BioPharm (acquired Oct-25): +15% QoQ; Geographic mix: NA 71.6% (+2% due to BioPharm), Europe 25.5%, RoW 2.9%.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling 'Tectonic' transformation model (5 customers, 2 moved to long-term); expanding beyond top-20 (active customers 73->91, $1mn+ contributors 41->53); capturing agency/CRO spend pools via GenAI; targeting mid-sized biotech launches; potential to create first $50mn+ customer (largest account) in FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin ~18.9%; FY26 margins impacted by 150bps from strategic investments (R&D >2% of revenue, GTM, domain talent); management guides margin recovery to prior highs in H2FY27 as investments absorb; outcome-based pricing protects productivity gains from AI.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly detailed; focus on inorganic growth (3 acquisitions in FY26: BioPharm, Warn, Cake) with ₹7,253mn outflow; organic capex embedded in R&D/tech platform development (Cortex, Content Super App).
capital allocation: Strong cash generation (OCF ₹6,508mn, FCF ₹6,065mn); Cash & Investments ₹15,385mn; Proposed final dividend ₹2.25/share (+12.5% YoY); continued investment in M&A for geographic/domain depth (Europe) and tech platforms.
risks & watch-items: Concentration risk (top-20 customers); AI commoditization of domain knowledge (management argues 3-5 year moat via proprietary data/workflows); Regulatory scrutiny on AI outputs (FDA warnings); Execution risk on scaling Tectonic; Forex volatility (hedging impact); Legal overhangs (TCPA settlement provision made, but future exposures deemed unlikely).
management quality / tone: Confident and excited (shift from 'cautiously optimistic' in FY26); emphasizes structural industry shift favoring Indegene; highlights 'category definition' rather than participation; transparent on one-offs and investment phase.
non-obvious takeaways: Revenue per employee jumped to $75k (from $56k 3 years ago) driven by AI + outcome pricing, not just offshoring; 'Agency-of-Record' pilot reduced creative cycle from 3 months to 3 days using synthetic KOLs and agentic workflows; TCPA lawsuit stems from FY19-20 fax usage (now inactive channel); DSO improved to 63 days (from 72), driving record cash flows despite M&A outflows.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
